deck: OpenIntM4TM2 libs.tech/klayout/tech/drc/run_drc.py, all decks, tiling mode, 4 threads
note: Known violations of the interposer PDK's own deck on the exported carrier.
The gate (adk-verify-carrier-drc) fails when any rule goes above these
counts or when a rule not listed here appears. It is a debt list, not a
waiver: every entry says what closing it needs. Nothing here is a defect
of the exporter; what is left is the reference board's routing.
Padc.b and Padc.e are absent on purpose: the gate delegates them, it does
not waive them. Both fired on this carrier (4748 markers each, all of them
the two attachment-pad pairs on U2), and U2 is attached with
vendorx_microbump, whose own rules allow 15 um space and 50 um pitch. The
deck cannot tell the dies apart, because vendorx_microbump lands on the
IHP Cu-pillar UBM by declaration (fab_anchor ihp_cupillar_anchor, layers
9/35 + 41/35 + 99/35) and draws the same 35 um passivation opening as
cupillar_opt1, and layers_def.drc derives CuPillarPad from exactly that
layer pair. So the deck runs PacTech Table 6.1 numbers over microbumps.
The interconnect PDK owns the per-method versions as IXN.b and IXN.e, and
the ADK assembly DRC checks this same geometry against 14.99 um and passes.
Measured: the two U2 pairs are 70.000 um centre to centre, 35.000 um edge
to edge, against the deck's 39.99 um threshold. U1 (cupillar_opt1) is
clean, its closest pair measuring 39.995 um edge to edge. Padc.e cannot
differ from Padc.b here by construction: (Padc_e 75 - Padc_a 35) - 0.01 is
the same 39.99 um as Padc_b 40 - 0.01. IHP also marks Padc.e as not
checked during DRC; the deck says so at 6_9_copperpillar.drc:31 and checks
it anyway. Delegation is conditional and needs proof: the gate reads the
pillar manifest beside the GDS and only delegates when a method there is
more permissive than the deck's numbers. A carrier with nothing but Cu
pillars keeps both rules, and a missing or unreadable manifest delegates
nothing, so the rules reappear as unknown and fail the gate.
For the record, what this baseline replaced: before the manufacturing-grid
work the same deck reported 18207 markers on this GDS, 8621 of them
offgrid (a 5 nm grid, and 155 of 174 cell instances were placed off it),
plus 35 metal-slit violations on the bond pads, 11 minimum-width and 2
angle markers. Those classes are now zero and must stay zero.
Then the exporter gained the notch heal (hyp_to_gds _heal_notches), which
closes sub-minimum-space gaps inside one piece of copper. That took TM2.b
from 40 to 3 and M5.b and M5.i from 1 each to zero, for 377 um2 of extra
TopMetal2 (0.05 percent of the layer) and no change in the merged polygon
count on any metal, i.e. nothing was bridged. Those classes must stay at
or below these counts.
Its patches are axis-aligned rectangles on purpose. A 45 degree chamfer on
them is legal in isolation and closes the same notches with less copper,
but it makes the merged copper pick up vertices off the 5 nm grid where a
chamfer meets the diagonal traces: 4 topmetal2_drw_Offgrid and 4
topmetal2_drw_Angle45 markers here, in flat, deep and tiling alike, none
of them at a drawn vertex. Re-run the offgrid and angle decks before
changing the patch shape.

TM2.b.why: Minimum TopMetal2 space or notch, 2 um. Was 40 before the exporter's notch heal; the 37 it closed were notches inside one piece of copper, mostly where a trace takes its first bend while still inside a round Cu-pillar pad and so leaves the pad almost tangentially. The 3 that remain all sit on the left edge of a 100 x 100 um wire-bond pad, which the heal stays out of on purpose: Pad.fR measures its 7 um exit band from the edge where the trace crosses the pad marker, so widening the trace there lengthens that edge and enlarges the band that has to stay covered. Healing them was measured and it moved Pad.fR_TM2 from 27 markers to 30 and its uncovered area from 450 to 466 um2, i.e. it traded a notch for a bigger exit violation. Closing these 3 is the same layout fix as Pad.fR_TM2: leave the bond pad orthogonally for 7 um before turning.

Pad.fR_TM2.why: Recommended, not mandatory (IHP marks recommendations with the R suffix): minimum TopMetal2 exit length of 7 um from a pad. Each marker is the corner of the 7 um exit band left uncovered because the trace leaves the bond pad diagonally. Appeared when the bond pads gained their dfpad and passivation opening, which is what makes them pads to the deck at all; before that the same pads were 35 hard Slt.c violations. Closing it means leaving each bond pad orthogonally for 7 um before turning, which also closes the 3 remaining TM2.b.
